text: Jitendra Kumar Maheshwari (born 29 June 1961) is a judge of the Supreme Court of India. He was previously chief justice of the Sikkim and Andhra Pradesh high courts and served as a judge of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Born in Joura, a small town in the Morena District of Madhya Pradesh, he graduated in arts in 1982 and obtained his LL.B. in 1985, followed by an LL.M. in 1991. He enrolled as an advocate with the Bar Council of Madhya Pradesh on 22 November 1985 and practiced in civil, criminal, constitutional, service, and tax matters. He was also an elected member of the M.P. State Bar Council. Appointed as an additional judge of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh on 25 November 2005, he was confirmed as a permanent judge on 25 November 2008. He served on various committees focused on improving the administration of the Madhya Pradesh High Court until 6 October 2019. He was elevated as Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court and assumed office on 7 October 2019, becoming the first Chief Justice of the newly established Andhra Pradesh High Court. In January 2021, the Supreme Court collegium swapped the chief justices of Andhra Pradesh and Sikkim high courts, after which Justice Maheshwari was transferred as Chief Justice of the High Court of Sikkim on 6 January 2021. In August 2021, the Supreme Court collegium, led by CJI N. V. Ramana, recommended his name along with eight other high court judges for appointment to the Supreme Court of India. He took oath as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India on 31 August 2021. As of 14 May 2025, he has become a member of the five-member Supreme Court collegium following the retirement of CJI Sanjiv Khanna.
